clauses.normalized_text: QUIC uses separate packet number spaces for each encryption level, except 0-RTT and all generations of 1-RTT keys use the same packet number space.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC uses separate packet number spaces for each encryption level, except 0-RTT and all generations of 1-RTT keys use the same packet number space.

clauses.raw_text: Congestion control and round-trip time (RTT) measurement are unified across packet number spaces.

clauses.normalized_text: TCP conflates transmission order at the sender with delivery order at the receiver, which results in retransmissions of the same data carrying the same sequence number, and consequently leads to “retransmission ambiguity”.
clauses.raw_text: TCP conflates transmission order at the sender with delivery order at the receiver, which results in retransmissions of the same data carrying the same sequence number, and consequently leads to “retransmission ambiguity”.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC separates the two: QUIC uses a packet number to indicate transmission order, and any application data is sent in one or more streams, with delivery order determined by stream offsets encoded within STREAM frames.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC separates the two: QUIC uses a packet number to indicate transmission order, and any application data is sent in one or more streams, with delivery order determined by stream offsets encoded within STREAM frames.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC’s packet number is strictly increasing within a packet number space, and directly encodes transmission order.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC’s packet number is strictly increasing within a packet number space, and directly encodes transmission order.

clauses.normalized_text: A higher packet number signifies that the packet was sent later, and a lower packet number signifies that the packet was sent earlier.
clauses.raw_text: A higher packet number signifies that the packet was sent later, and a lower packet number signifies that the packet was sent earlier.

clauses.normalized_text: When a packet containing ack-eliciting frames is detected lost, QUIC rebundles necessary frames in a new packet with a new packet number, removing ambiguity about which packet is acknowledged when an ACK is received.
clauses.raw_text: When a packet containing ack-eliciting frames is detected lost, QUIC rebundles necessary frames in a new packet with a new packet number, removing ambiguity about which packet is acknowledged when an ACK is received.

clauses.normalized_text: Consequently, more accurate RTT measurements can be made, spurious retransmissions are trivially detected, and mechanisms such as Fast Retransmit can be applied universally, based only on packet number.

clauses.normalized_text: This design point significantly simplifies loss detection mechanisms for QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC ACKs contain information that is similar to TCP SACK, but QUIC does not allow any acked packet to be reneged, greatly simplifying implementations on both sides and reducing memory pressure on the sender.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC ACKs contain information that is similar to TCP SACK, but QUIC does not allow any acked packet to be reneged, greatly simplifying implementations on both sides and reducing memory pressure on the sender.

clauses.raw_text: QUIC ACKs explicitly encode the delay incurred at the receiver between when a packet is received and when the corresponding ACK is sent.

clauses.normalized_text: This allows the receiver of the ACK to adjust for receiver delays, specifically the delayed ack timer, when estimating the path RTT.

clauses.raw_text: QUIC SHOULD delay sending acknowledgements in response to packets, but MUST NOT excessively delay acknowledgements of ack-eliciting packets.

clauses.raw_text: Specifically, implementations MUST attempt to enforce a maximum ack delay to avoid causing the peer spurious timeouts.

clauses.normalized_text: A packet is declared lost if it meets all the following conditions:
